name: Menus and shopping lists
intro: Where a recipe becomes a list and family sync holds up in the store, and where sync breaks and drops items.

apps.title: Plan to Eat
apps.verdict: One of the strongest meal planning apps out there: import recipes from any website, auto-generate a consolidated grocery list from your weekly menu, scale portions, and sync with Instacart.
apps.loved: Import recipes by URL from any site or Instagram Reels, automatic portion scaling, one combined grocery list from multiple recipes, ingredient tagging and search, cross-platform web and mobile
apps.weak: Importing from Facebook comments or TikTok requires manual link copying, keyboard covers the notes field when adding items, no standardized units of measurement
apps.whoFor: People who take meal planning seriously and want one place for recipes, weekly menus, and a grocery list

quotes.text: This is a godsend. I love being able to see a recipe online, upload it into the app, and have the ingredients automatically added to my shopping list. LIFE CHANGING!!

I really enjoy this app, but I still have some challenges importing recipes from Facebook and TikTok. When recipes are in a facebook comment, you can't just import the recipe. You have to go into the comment with the recipe, manually copy the link to the comment and then go to the app and import t

I've been using this app for years. It is so helpful and user-friendly. It's easy to copy recipes from websites. Then as you plan your recipes for the week, you can select those dates to generate a shopping list.

We use it every day. It is so easy to use. The ability to pull recipes from all over and have the app organize them is amazing. It's only my husband and I so we often adjust the portions from the original recipe which the app does for you.

apps.title: AnyList: Grocery Shopping List
apps.verdict: The top pick in this category for combining lists and recipes: powerful sync, recipe import from websites, and Alexa integration. Weak spots are data privacy and occasional sign-in problems after switching devices.
apps.loved: Seamless sync across all devices. Import recipes from websites and auto-generate grocery lists. Alexa integration for voice-adding items. Store and category organization. Rock-solid reliability for years.
apps.weak: List data ended up with Amazon without explicit user consent. Recovering an account after a device switch is a nightmare and support is unresponsive. Alexa integration has degraded since Amazon made changes.
apps.whoFor: People who seriously plan meals for the week, maintain a recipe library, and want a shared grocery list with a partner. The best option in the category for active households.

quotes.text: AnyList has allowed me to organize our meals more efficiently and to not buy extra stuff at the grocery stores. My wife and I cannot get along without it.

This is a great app for planning meal and automatically adding the ingredients to your shopping list. The only downside is that I would like to be able to track my spending as I am going through the store by barcoding the prices to make sure I am staying within budget.

apps.title: Our Groceries Shopping List
apps.verdict: A mature shared grocery list app with real-time sync, Apple Watch support, and Alexa voice input. Recent UI updates have frustrated many long-time users, but the core feature still works reliably.
apps.loved: Real-time sync across devices. Great Apple Watch integration. Store section organization. Item autocomplete. Customizable categories.
apps.weak: Alexa integration is broken for some users after an update. The latest redesign moved things around and made common actions harder. Limited color label options and some are hard to read.
apps.whoFor: Couples and families who share a grocery list, Apple Watch users, and anyone who wants collaborative planning without a subscription.

quotes.text: This is a great app for shopping lists. Everything works perfectly, especially between iPhone and Apple Watch which is a rarity. And it's free!
The Our Grocery Shopping list App is great. I can list the stores I shop at and enter the items in the order I walk through the store.

apps.title: MealBoard - Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A thoughtful meal planner with a recipe library, grocery list generation, and inventory tracking. Despite a dated interface, it remains a favorite tool for people who take weekly menu planning seriously.
apps.loved: Recipes, menus, and grocery lists all work together as one system, website recipe import, inventory tracking for pantry items, long-term developer support and no subscription required
apps.weak: Import does not work with every site and often needs manual cleanup, the interface looks visually dated, no import from YouTube or social media, device sync occasionally fails, no shared access for couples
apps.whoFor: People who seriously maintain a cooking archive and plan menus for the week and do not care about modern design

quotes.text: I can't seem to import recipes with this latest update. The auto import has just stopped working completely, and when I try to import manually, I get a spinning wheel of death and the app gets caught on 'processing ingredients'. Super disappointing, as the ease of importing recipes to create grocery

apps.title: Prospre - Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A solid macro-based meal planner that auto-generates a plan and grocery list, but strictly limits keto diets and non-standard macronutrient ratios.
apps.loved: Automatically generates a meal plan based on your macros and preferences, the free version gives you full functionality, grocery list is built from the plan
apps.weak: Refuses to build a plan if macros fall outside its recommended range (keto, high-protein diets), no metric system support, allergens are sometimes ignored
apps.whoFor: People with a standard macro balance who want a ready-made weekly meal plan without doing it manually

quotes.text: I finally found an app that has everything I was looking for. The meals that they provide are based off my macros and i have not had one disappointing meal yet. I've owned it for almost 2 months. And the way they make everything so easy and organized is amazing!

I put in my macros targets for keto and it said I was outside of their 'recommended range' for fat so it didn't give me any meals. Pretty much useless unless your macros fall inside their 'recommended range'.
Submitted gluten and wheat allergy and it's still putting bread on my meal plan.

apps.title: Lists To do
apps.verdict: A simple and reliable to-do list that many people use as a grocery list. Not built for groceries specifically, but it works steadily and is genuinely free. The main pain points are occasional disappearing items and a clunky reordering feature.
apps.loved: Truly free with no hidden limits. Quick to add tasks and photos. Works without an account.
apps.weak: List items disappear when the app is closed, a recurring bug for multiple users. No easy drag-to-reorder. No time-based reminders in the free version.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants the simplest free list possible and is not looking for grocery-specific features like categories or recipes.

apps.title: Meal Planner & Weekly Menu
apps.verdict: A visually appealing meal planner with solid structure, but recipe ingredients are not automatically transferred to the grocery list and there is a language bug that displays Dutch instead of English.
apps.loved: Pleasant design that motivates you to stick to your plan, easy recipe adding
apps.weak: Recipe ingredients do not automatically populate the grocery list, interface language bug shows Dutch instead of English, no collaborative editing for families
apps.whoFor: People who want a visually clean weekly meal plan without deep analytics

quotes.text: I like the look of the app and it was fairly easy to add recipes, although the failure to default to initial caps and to move to the next item on return is a problem. But the reason this is unusable for me is that when I add recipes to the calendar, the ingredients are not automatically entered on t

apps.title: Recipe Keeper
apps.verdict: The best recipe organizer in its class: browser import, photos, and Instagram import all work cleanly. But the monetization model hides the real price (phone plus computer equals around fifty dollars), and there is no family sharing.
apps.loved: One-click recipe import from any source, flexible portion scaling, grocery list creation from your menu
apps.weak: Separate purchase required for each platform without a clear warning upfront, no family sharing inside the household, some users have lost recipes
apps.whoFor: Someone who stores recipes only on their own phone and does not plan to share them with family members

apps.title: List Ease: Shared Grocery List
apps.verdict: A long-time veteran of the category with solid store and category organization, but it has degraded in recent months with frequent freezes and sync failures between family members.
apps.loved: Flexible sorting by store aisle order. Per-item price tracking. Barcode scanning. Years of stability before recent updates.
apps.weak: The app freezes regularly mid-use. Sync between devices breaks and does not recover even after contacting support. Social login is required for shared list features.
apps.whoFor: Users who need a list with flexible categories and price tracking and are okay with occasional freezes.

quotes.text: Have used this app for years to organize store runs. Pros easy to use, ability to check off items placed in cart. Cons the app is unable to categorize even the simplest things like apples, lettuce even though I buy them almost every store run.

apps.title: Spillt: Recipe & Meal Plan App
apps.verdict: A social recipe planner with a free model and easy Instagram import, but it runs unstably with frequent crashes and ads injected right into recipe steps.
apps.loved: One place for recipes from any source, one-tap import from Instagram, a social feed without like counters, grocery list generated from a recipe
apps.weak: Frequent crashes on launch, ads inserted directly into recipe steps and sometimes cannot be closed, iPad version is not properly adapted
apps.whoFor: Cooking enthusiasts who want a free app with a social feature and can tolerate occasional crashes

apps.title: Pantry Check - Grocery List
apps.verdict: A serious pantry tracker with a barcode scanner and expiration date tracking, but there is no cross-device sync and no Android support.
apps.loved: Fast barcode scanning, expiration date reminders, helps avoid duplicate purchases
apps.weak: No shared access across devices and no Android version, rare cases of complete data loss, support does not respond for weeks
apps.whoFor: Organized households that want to know exactly what is in the kitchen and avoid unnecessary spending

quotes.text: Knowing exactly what's in your pantry and when it'll expire is a game changer. Now, I understand my eating habits a lot better and can budget almost to perfection without looking at the receipt.

This could be a really useful app if I could log into my account on multiple devices. Unfortunately I added items in my pantry on my iPad and found out too late that I was unable to log into my account on my iPhone.

Amazing App it has all the features you need! I purchased the yearly subscription for 2,000 products because it's a great way to keep track of the products that I have at home in our pantry and also to help my parents keep track of what they have in stock and also to avoid making unnecessary purchas

apps.title: Flipp: Shop Grocery Deals
apps.verdict: A supermarket flyer aggregator that genuinely helps deal hunters. The main limitation is coverage: if your store is not in the database, the app is useless.
apps.loved: All store ads in one place. Fast search to see which store has a specific item on sale this week. Watchlist notifications for deals on items you track.
apps.weak: Search returns irrelevant results and items from stores outside your area. Many regional chains are not in the database. In-app prices sometimes do not match store prices.
apps.whoFor: Budget-conscious shoppers who plan trips across multiple stores to get the best prices for the week.

apps.title: Shopping List - Grocery & Todo
apps.verdict: An extremely simple grocery list with no extras, fast and clear to use, but there is no undo for deleted items and only one list is supported, which is a dealbreaker for some users.
apps.loved: Instant use without sign-up, minimalist interface, one tap to check off items
apps.weak: No way to undo accidentally deleting the entire list, only one list for everything, items sometimes duplicate with no explanation, ads appeared in newer versions
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants to open an app and just add milk without dealing with settings, categories, or cloud sync

quotes.text: Love this shopping app, check off when I pick up the item and quick review before I check out to make sure I didn't miss anything. Plus, no more impulse buying is saving me money in this hard time.

I WISH you would have a 'are you sure you want to delete' question before your checked items delete!! I use this list as my ongoing grocery list simply by unchecking the items I need to get at the store this week. MORE than once I have hit the trash can by accident because it is so close to the

apps.title: Bring! Grocery Shopping List
apps.verdict: A clean and attractive shared list app with a simple interface, but sync is unreliable and the app has gradually degraded: Apple Watch support was dropped and the Alexa integration is broken.
apps.loved: Clean and intuitive interface, easy onboarding with no learning curve, good icon and visual category support, reliable for years for some users
apps.weak: Sync deletes items instead of merging duplicates when two people add the same thing, Apple Watch support was removed, Alexa integration is broken, Siri adding does not work despite being advertised
apps.whoFor: People who value a clean minimalist interface and basic family sync without demanding reliability for high-stakes scenarios

quotes.text: I bought this app to also use it on apple watch but after a few months it lost apple watch support.

This app on my phone and watch doesn't communicate correctly. After grocery shopping is done and items cleared off of my watch app, I then have to clear the items off of my phone app. Just now, syncing up my watch and phone for grocery items, it cleared out all but 2 items in the app.

apps.title: FitGenie: Macro & Food Tracker
apps.verdict: A macro tracker with an adaptive algorithm for your goals, but it is slow, crashes frequently when entering data quickly, and does not sync with other fitness apps.
apps.loved: Algorithm automatically recalculates macros based on progress, suggests meal ideas for the remaining macros in the day, clean interface
apps.weak: Crashes on quick-add, no integration with Apple Health or MyFitnessPal, weak food database for Australia and the UK, every action requires a network request
apps.whoFor: Athletes and bodybuilders who want precise macro targeting without manual configuration

quotes.text: FINALLY. An app that HELPS me to reach my goals by adjusting the macros. And they also provide meal ideas to help reach the rest of your macros. Love love love this app!

apps.title: eMeals - Healthy Meal Plans
apps.verdict: A genuinely functional meal planner with ready-made recipes and an automatic list for Walmart or Instacart. Recipe quality is basic, billing is opaque, and the app pushes Walmart on every screen.
apps.loved: Automatic grocery list from selected recipes for the week. Walmart and Instacart integration for one-tap ordering. Wide selection of meal plans for different diets.
apps.weak: The grocery list multiplies ingredient quantities by the number of recipes instead of combining them. Recipes are bland with minimal seasoning. Walmart ads on every screen even for paid subscribers. No renewal notifications and charges happen without warning.
apps.whoFor: Busy families who need a ready-made weekly plan without picking recipes themselves and who already shop at Walmart.

quotes.text: We love this app. We've tried other options over the years, but come back to eMeals every time! I do wish there was a meal prep mode that would easily tell you what and how to prep in advance!

The app will add dozens of random ingredients to the shopping list. I had 9 12 oz bags of broccoli when I needed 3. 9 bell peppers when I needed 3. The list goes on and on. It's to the point where it's completely unusable.

apps.title: Grocery List: Out of Milk
apps.verdict: A solid old-school grocery list with a pantry section and shared access that worked reliably for years, but sync has started glitching, ads appeared without warning, and support has gone silent.
apps.loved: Purchase history for quick list repeats, pantry section with transfer to grocery list, Apple Watch support
apps.weak: Sync between two users is unreliable, barcode scanner is broken, ads appeared in the free version, data sometimes disappears after updates
apps.whoFor: Small families who want a shared grocery list without a subscription or unnecessary features

quotes.text: I downloaded the app as I was looking for a good app to not only help me create a shopping list but organizing it by store departments to make my grocery shopping easier. Yesterday I had a list of 20-25 items and halfway through my shopping the app deleted my entire list with no way to recover it.

apps.title: Shoppylist - Grocery List
apps.verdict: A veteran grocery list app with a devoted following that gets let down periodically by updates that break sharing and item deletion.
apps.loved: Low learning curve, support for multiple lists, long-time users keep coming back for years
apps.weak: Sync between devices breaks after every major update, the widget only shows four items, there is no way to clear the list
apps.whoFor: Families who need a simple shared list with no extras and can tolerate occasional bugs

quotes.text: Once I check off the items I purchased I can't figure out a way where I can reuse the same items again because I buy the same things over and over again. It's down a huge list and uncheck them all. I wish there was a way

apps.title: Vegan Bowls: Plant Based Meals
apps.verdict: A vegan recipe app from the Coconut Bowls brand with a built-in grocery list, but some users cannot open it at all and the recipe library is small for the annual subscription price.
apps.loved: Beautiful recipe photos, linked grocery list, recipes are reportedly genuinely tasty and approachable
apps.weak: App fails to launch for some users on iOS, too few recipes for the annual subscription price, heavy bias toward oil-based dishes with no filter, the snacks section duplicates other sections
apps.whoFor: Fans of the Coconut Bowls brand and people just starting out with plant-based eating who want simple and visually appealing recipes

apps.title: ReciMe: Recipes & Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A technically capable recipe aggregator with auto-import from any source, but a monetization model built around a forced trial and a hidden subscription seriously undermines trust. The product works, there is no feature fraud, but the billing practices are predatory.
apps.loved: Flawless recipe import from websites, videos, and photos. Auto-generated grocery list from recipes. Excellent library organization and search.
apps.weak: Subscription does not go through the App Store, so users cannot see or cancel it through system settings. The 5 to 8 recipe limit before the paywall is very low. Import occasionally fails.
apps.whoFor: People who actively collect recipes from the internet and are willing to pay a subscription, but only if they understand the terms before signing up.

quotes.text: If I could have dreamt up the most perfect app it still would not have been as good as this one is. Incredible ! Not a detail missed. Any recipe in any form, website, social media, cook book or handwritten from your grandmother gets imported correctly and seamlessly.

apps.title: Grocery List with Sync
apps.verdict: A grocery list with cross-device sync and purchase memory. The concept works, but sync breaks periodically and new subscription restrictions have frustrated long-time users.
apps.loved: Purchase history memory, Apple Watch support, multiple lists for different stores
apps.weak: Cross-device sync is unreliable even on a paid plan, aggressive subscription banners, old lists get lost after updates
apps.whoFor: Couples and families who want a shared list, if the sync is actually working

quotes.text: My wife and I have been using this app for a while, but we've been running into sync issues that are happening with increasing frequency. I'll add something to our shared list, but my wife's list doesn't update. Or vice versa. And there's no way to force a sync.
I uploaded the app to my Apple Watch. It's really handy when shopping, and make crossing-off items already selected.

In case you suddenly find the time to get grocery shopping in, you have your list already with you on your phone. No more forgetting that one thing because you forgot to bring your list. Everything is super easy to add or take off and it remembers what you got the last time.
The app is easy to use, remembers past list items and lets users create multiple lists for different stores.

apps.title: Total Plus:Shopping Calculator
apps.verdict: A simple in-store calculator that tracks your running total with tax. It solves exactly one problem and does it reasonably well, but crashes and pushy review requests get in the way.
apps.loved: Automatic tax rate detection via location, quick per-item total with tax, simple and clear interface with no clutter
apps.weak: Ten-item limit in the free version, no single combined list across multiple stores, frequent crashes when entering a price, aggressive repeat prompts to rate the app within the same session
apps.whoFor: Shoppers who want to track their budget in the store and see a running total with tax in real time

quotes.text: This app is one of my most used apps. It's important that I know what my total will be at the end of shopping, and also see how much each item will be after taxes. This app does that for me. Love it quick and simple.

The app is ok, but why can't we see the total of our shopping cart? I'm sure I'm like most others and mark things off as I purchase them in the store, why can't I see my total without selecting every single item?

apps.title: Lists To-do
apps.verdict: A minimalist list organizer that handles simple tasks well, but crashes periodically and loses data with no response from the developer.
apps.loved: Easy to add and organize lists by category, ability to print the list
apps.weak: Recurring crashes for some users with data loss, no sub-items or nested lists, developer does not respond to support requests
apps.whoFor: People who need a lightweight grocery or to-do list with no extra features

apps.title: Meal Planner & Grocery List
apps.verdict: A linked meal planner and grocery list with fast recipe import, but it suffers from interface freezes and illogical UX: you cannot add an existing recipe to a plan without creating a new one.
apps.loved: Fast recipe import from websites, auto-generated grocery list from the weekly plan, can share the plan with a partner
apps.weak: App freezes and becomes unresponsive, you cannot add a saved recipe to the plan in one step, no checkbox feature for marking items as purchased
apps.whoFor: Families who need a connected meal plan and grocery list for the week, if missing checkboxes in the list is not a dealbreaker

apps.title: Visual Grocery: Shopping List
apps.verdict: A visual grocery list with item photos and sync that is slowly degrading: image search from the web was removed and ads are now impossible to dismiss.
apps.loved: Visual item cards with photos, sync with others, easy sorting by category
apps.weak: Web image search was removed without explanation, ads block the interface and cannot be closed, data has been lost several times after updates
apps.whoFor: People who want a visual list with their own photo library of items and can tolerate aggressive ads

apps.title: Grocery Gadget
apps.verdict: A veteran of the category with a rich history going back to Palm Pilot, but development has effectively stopped: sync breaks at the worst possible moment, support does not respond, and there have been no meaningful updates in years.
apps.loved: Flexible organization across multiple store lists, aisle sorting, barcode and photo support, extensive accumulated lists from years of use
apps.weak: Sync between two people's phones regularly stops working right in the store, support does not respond to requests, no significant updates since 2019, search sometimes shows ads instead of the item you need
apps.whoFor: Long-time users with large accumulated lists who have nowhere to migrate and are willing to live with unreliable sync

quotes.text: Partner and I have used this app for years, but the app is constantly plagued with 'internal server errors.' We each spent a long time on our respective phones in creating a large list. When I arrived at the grocery store, I found that the list would not sync due to an 'internal server error.'

Grocery Gadget is essential for my monthly shopping. I live in a rural area and travel to the city monthly to shop at Costco and other stores as needed. I shop for myself and 2-3 others. This app makes these shopping trips easy and efficient. I wouldn't be without it.

apps.title: SideСhef: Easy Cooking Recipes
apps.verdict: A recipe assistant with a beautiful step-by-step guide, but crashes, broken web import, and a forced migration from another app have pushed away loyal users.
apps.loved: Step-by-step instructions with photos, grocery list generation from recipes, clean design
apps.weak: Frequent crashes and freezes, Walmart cart integration is broken, BudgetBytes users lost their recipe history, link import is unstable
apps.whoFor: Beginner cooks willing to tolerate instability for the sake of a large recipe library

apps.title: Grocery Buddy: Fast Checklist
apps.verdict: A new grocery list app with auto-sorting by category and item photos, but the release is rough: data gets wiped after updates and the deals feature does not work for anyone.
apps.loved: Automatic sorting by department, item photo search, saves past purchases without retyping
apps.weak: Entire list wiped after an update, multiple attempts needed to add a single item, deals never appear for any user
apps.whoFor: People who want something smarter than a notes app and are okay with instability

quotes.text: This app has made my grocery shopping stress free and easy! Love how it tells me what aisle my products is found! Highly recommend!

apps.title: Grocery & Shopping List Pro
apps.verdict: A grocery list app with item photos and shared access, but aggressive ads with hidden close buttons and data loss after updates make it unfit for regular use.
apps.loved: Ability to add a photo of any item, multiple lists for different stores, real-time family access
apps.weak: Ads in Chinese with no close button, hidden and moving ad close buttons, sync breaks after updates and wipes all data, barcode scanner does not work on branded products
apps.whoFor: Users willing to pay to turn off ads and who do not need reliable data transfer between devices

apps.title: Cooklist: Pantry Meals Recipes
apps.verdict: The most ambitious concept in the category: scans receipts, tracks your pantry, and builds a grocery list from what you have left. But store sync breaks, the price is hidden until the very end, and bugs keep piling up.
apps.loved: Receipt and barcode scanning, expiration date tracking, recipe suggestions based on what is already in the fridge
apps.weak: A $10 per month subscription is hidden until the end of onboarding, Kroger and Amazon sync periodically fails, customer support is unreachable when there are payment issues
apps.whoFor: An organized home cook willing to pay for full pantry control, if the app is running reliably

quotes.text: I'm disabled and have some memory issues. I just discovered your app and scanned everything I had, and out of 500 or so items I only had to enter about 6 manually. It's been a great help with eating and budgeting.

I really wanted to love this app, it was great at first with helping me keep track of my groceries and even using up almost expired food… but the Kroger app, the main store I use, needed to update my login info everytime I logged into app.

Great app, but you NEED to add a feature to scan virtual receipts!! Most people don't shop in person often anymore. There's no reason I shouldn't be able to add orders using e-receipts from doordash, shipt, and other unsupported grocery delivery apps. SUPER frustrating.

I used to love this app. I loved it so much that I didn't mind paying the yearly subscription price. It uploaded all of my purchases and it also helped me cut down wasted food AND helped me 'shop' from my cabinet. This app hands down saved me so much money on my grocery bill. Then all of a sudden, K

The ability to scan in grocery receipts, recipes, and so on is great. The user interface is sometimes not very intuitive. The big lack in my eyes is the inability to integrate easily with other apps, especially laptop apps, and the inability to easily export user recipes into other formats.

apps.title: Grocery List - Listonic
apps.verdict: A shared grocery list app that has degraded due to aggressive ads: banners cover the entire list while you are shopping and sponsored items get added to your list without your permission.
apps.loved: Real-time family list sync, automatic category sorting, multiple lists for different stores
apps.weak: Full-screen ads cover the list while shopping, sponsored items are added to your personal list, AI categorization broke sorting and dumps everything into 'other', periodic crashes after updates
apps.whoFor: Families who are okay with ads in exchange for free sync, or willing to pay for a subscription to get a clean experience

quotes.text: I live with my father and brother, and since our schedules are so different, it's hard to go shopping at the same time. The fact that we can all update the list and access it from our phones has been a game changer.
They added some bull AI element and suddenly it's incapable of basic categorization. It still works but I'm nearly done with it dumping every entry into 'other'.

apps.title: Grocery List ◎
apps.verdict: An offline grocery list with multi-store and category support that falls apart on the basics: no sync between your own phone and iPad, shared access for couples costs extra, and the UX is not intuitive.
apps.loved: Support for multiple stores with separate lists, flexible category customization, developer responds quickly to support requests
apps.weak: No sync between devices for the same user, shared access requires a separate purchase, no list search, no button to delete completed items, app automatically creates new items without user input
apps.whoFor: Solo shoppers who shop at several different stores and do not need sync or shared access

apps.title: BigOven Recipes & Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A massive recipe database with an organizer and meal planner, but ads cover recipe instructions even after paying for Pro, saved recipes disappear, and canceling a subscription is a battle.
apps.loved: Millions of recipes in one place, ability to add your own, folder organization, offline access
apps.weak: Ads persist after buying Pro, recipes and folders disappear without warning, customer support does not answer calls, subscription cancellation is blocked
apps.whoFor: Someone who needs a huge recipe library and does not care about the reliability of their own stored data

apps.title: List Maker ◎
apps.verdict: A visually appealing list organizer with icons and colors that has gradually been choked by a paywall and technical failures: lists delete themselves, the app stops opening, and password reset does not work.
apps.loved: Wide selection of icons, colors, and fonts for styling lists, simple and clear for basic needs, saves data on reinstall
apps.weak: Lists spontaneously delete themselves or get created empty, app stops opening after updates, password recovery does not work, shared access is paid-only, aggressive paywall
apps.whoFor: Solo users who want a good-looking list with no reliability requirements and no need for shared access

apps.title: Simple Grocery List
apps.verdict: A simple grocery list with a solid basic concept that has not been updated in years and has an unfixed critical bug: a persistent sync popup appears even when the app is on a single device.
apps.loved: Simple and fast, support for multiple lists, drag-to-reorder items, basic functionality with no clutter
apps.weak: A popup about list changes on another device appears even when the app is on only one phone, no updates in years, item duplication on manual entry, no aisle grouping
apps.whoFor: Someone looking for a simple list with no extras and willing to live with an unfixed sync bug

apps.title: Grocery - Smart Shopping List
apps.verdict: An app with an ambitious feature set (inventory, recipes, smart clearing) that works unreliably in practice: freezes, crashes, broken sync, and a smart grouping tool that duplicates items instead of merging them.
apps.loved: The idea of combining inventory and grocery list in one place, aisle sorting, multi-store support, no ads in the base version
apps.weak: App is slow on any device, smart clearing duplicates items instead of merging, Mac version crashes constantly, app periodically stops opening, support is unreachable
apps.whoFor: Patient users willing to invest time in setup in exchange for no ads and the inventory concept

quotes.text: I would tell it what recipes I want to cook, check off things I already have, and it would make one clean list. I had smart Clean Up on and I am still getting 6 different 'egg' list items. I try to rename them wi
There is a bug where the total doesn't update no matter what you put on the list. Tried to put in a ticket inside the app.

apps.title: Menu Planner
apps.verdict: Once a decent menu planner with budget calculations, now effectively abandoned: crashes on print, import is broken, no updates in three years.
apps.loved: Ingredient price entry with budget calculation, flexible meal categories, suitable for planning menus weeks ahead
apps.weak: Printing recipes crashes the app on iOS 18, recipe import by link does not work, barcode scanner finds nothing, developer is unreachable
apps.whoFor: People who plan menus manually and do not depend on printing or recipe import

quotes.text: I love that I can input the prices for the ingredients and then after I make a shopping list, it will tell me how much it should cost.

apps.title: SIMPLE Shopping List + To Do
apps.verdict: An ultra-minimalist list with no categories, no photo support, and no real sharing, which was also broken by a recent update that shuffled item order and added a forced subscription.
apps.loved: Easy to add items, no account required, takes up minimal space
apps.weak: List order randomly reshuffles after an update, sharing only works as a text message, no printing, subscription is pushed without warning
apps.whoFor: Solo users with no need for shared access, willing to accept no categories and ongoing instability

quotes.text: Something changed in this app about a couple of months ago. From being a brilliant and useful app for shopping has become almost unusable. Too frequently I can't open my list. apps.title: Grocery Gadget Lite
apps.verdict: A functional grocery list with store sorting that was ruined by aggressive ads: they appear right in the middle of shopping and cannot be dismissed for several seconds.
apps.loved: Sorting items by aisle and store, simple interface for maintaining an ongoing list
apps.weak: Forced audio ads with no close button for users who previously paid, periodic total data loss, no sync between devices
apps.whoFor: People willing to pay for a clean ad-free experience and confident in stable data storage

apps.title: Grocery list. Shopping list
apps.verdict: A grocery list app with categories and a pantry feature built on dishonest monetization: it has locked users out of their own data multiple times without warning.
apps.loved: Department-based categorization, multi-list by store, pantry tracking
apps.weak: Bait-and-switch: free features become paid without notice and block access to existing data, sharing and sync do not work
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone under the current monetization policy

apps.title: Grocery/Shopping List Pro
apps.verdict: A basic grocery list app with preset categories that the developer broke with a design update. Before that it was already suffering from a data-wiping crash and aggressive rating prompts on first launch.
apps.loved: Preset item categories save time during initial setup, left-swipe to delete works as expected
apps.weak: Crash that wipes all data during list entry, mandatory review prompt on the very first use, an update broke the familiar interface, developer responds rudely to criticism in reviews, no cross-device sync
apps.whoFor: Not recommended in its current state

apps.title: ShopShop - Shopping List
apps.verdict: A cult minimalist grocery list with a 15-year history, but abandoned by its developer: editing and reordering items crashes the app on every modern iOS version.
apps.loved: Extremely simple interface like a paper list, multiple stores, autocomplete from history
apps.weak: Last update was six years ago, any editing causes a crash, no real-time sharing, data resets periodically
apps.whoFor: Only for existing users with an old iPhone and a list already filled in. No reason for new users to try it.

apps.title: Grocery Shopping To Do List
apps.verdict: A grocery list app built around the concept of a reusable master list, but entirely broken: editing any item causes a crash and the developer has not fixed this bug in years.
apps.loved: The master list concept for reuse across shopping trips, clean interface with no ads
apps.weak: Editing any item crashes the app (a bug that has existed for years), no real-time sharing, app freezes offline
apps.whoFor: Hard to recommend to anyone given the unfixed critical bug

apps.title: Shopping List - Simple & Easy
apps.verdict: A basic grocery list completely ruined by aggressive ads: popups block the interface right in the store, and scam warnings about your phone being hacked appear in the ad flow.
apps.loved: Simple list structure by store, works offline
apps.weak: Ads cover the list and cannot be closed, scam popups about device hacking, no cross-device sync, cannot rename a list
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in its current state

scenarios.name: Weekly planners
scenarios.job: Build a week’s menu from their own recipes, get one consolidated shopping list, and close it with a single order or store run

scenarios.name: Macro trackers
scenarios.job: Plan a day’s diet around a specific protein, fat and carb ratio and get the grocery list that delivers on that plan

scenarios.name: Deal hunters
scenarios.job: Find out which store has a specific item cheaper this week and plan a multi-store route around the best prices
